                                          Further Information On UFO In The Road
  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Tue, 3 Jan 2006 19:49:34 -0500
  Fwd Date: Wed, 04 Jan 2006 09:22:21 -0500
  Subject: Further Information On UFO In The Road

  -----
  The Journal of Hispanic Ufology
  January 3, 2006
  Source: El Liberal Digital
  Date: Tuesday, January 3, 2006
  Loreto Woman Photographed What She Thought Was A UFO
  LORETO - Miryan Coronel is one of the many residents of Loreto
  who return home to celebrate the holidays with family. She has
  been living in Chubut for over 20 years and on December 29
  undertook her yearly journey, not knowing that 19 hours after
  leaving, she and her fellow travelers would be witnesses to the
  takeoff of what she described as an unidentified flying object.
  According to the protagonist, the event took place on the road
  linking the provinces of Cordoba and San Luis in the vicinity of
  Mount Uritorco in the middle of the Cordoba mountains. This site
  is well-known as the location for many events related to the
  manifestation of strange lights associated to extraterrestrial
  craft.
  "At two o'clock in the morning we boarded the bus belonging to
  the Andesmar bus line with my sons Santiago,8, and Angel, 4. We
  occupied seats 40,41 and 42. After nearly 20 hours of travel,
  the first stars began to appear through the bus's windows. The
  time was around 21:45 hours," Miryan notes, later adding:
  "Suddenly the bus stopped, and when I looked down the aisle, I
  saw an immense light in the middle of the road."
  "I immediately jumped out of the seat and saw that my sons were
  asleep, along with many passengers. I moved to the front of the
  bus and saw the cone-shaped light in the middle of the road, and
  got off with the bus drivers and a passenger from Salta who had
  a camcorder. At no time did I feel fear -- on the contrary, I
  was engulfed by a sensation of peace and curiosity, to the
  extent that I began taking photos with my cellphone camera. When
  I tried to get closer, one of the bus drivers held me back," she
  explained.
  Proceeding with her account, Miryan says: "Suddenly the object,
  that was enveloped in a bluish white light, began spinning like
  a top and rising vertically, lighting up the landscape as though
  it was daytime. In the measure that the giant spinning top rose,
  it gave off multicolored lights in intense phosphorescent tones
  before vanishing into a brilliant spot. I immediately began
  perceiving a smell of heated metal, combining with a very
  particular odor similar to sulfur."
  According to Miryan, the event lasted only a few minutes and no
  sound was heard. Upon returning to the bus, they exchanged
  remarks with the people who shared the experience and with the
  drivers, who said that they had always seen strange lights in
  the area, but nothing to comapre with the experience on the
  night of December 29, 2005.
  "After the chat I returned to my seat and fell into a deep


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m04-011.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:08]
Further Information On UFO In The Road

  sleep. I slept until we reached the Loreto bus terminal. They
  had to wake me up to get me off the bus," said the passenger of
  this highly unusual journey."
  -----
  Translation (c) 2005 Scott Corrales
  Institute of Hispanic Ufology (IHU)
  Special thanks to Christian Quintero, Planeta UFO

  Dick and List
  For what it's worth I think Cathy's formalisation of the issue
  was very interesting and well expressed, and the language of
  dynamical systems seems a useful tool for thinking about it.
  >According to the historical record, Fermi simply threw out the
  >question "Where is everyone?" informally, and the utterly
  >unscientific expression has received far more attention and
  >almost reverent respect than it deserves.
  Well this was why Cathy's expression of the idea was
  interesting. It wasn't just "thrown out" but was an attempt to
  generalise the problem in terms of dynamical principles that are
  widely applied to thinking about problems of analogous kinds. If
  our criticism of Fermi is that he didn't bother to formalise his
  notion carefully, how can we criticise Cathy because she does?
  >It's premise clearly
  >is that no one has visited us, but where is any evidence that
  >Fermi actually studied, or was even aware of, substantial UFO
  >reports as possible evidence of ET visits?
  Fermi's question remains interesting even though we take UFO


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m04-013.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:10]
Re: ETH Does Not Solve The Fermi Paradox - Shough

  reports seriously. Even if we strongly suspect something
  analogous to ET visitation as the nearest notion within our
  scientific purview, this doesn't mean that we know enough about
  the UFOs or the cosmos to grasp what this really means. Fermi's
  "paradox" isn't just about "Why aren't they here?" but about
  "Why aren't they _everywhere_".
  "They" (whoever or whatever "they" are in our particular case)
  could well be here, and Fermi still has a point. Why don't we
  appear to see astrophysical evidence of Dyson spheres, or other
  massive engineering on planetary, stellar, or even galactic
  scales? Why isn't observable space saturated with material and
  informational artefacts of all kinds?
  Not that we _should_ see such things; but we _might_, given the
  potential for billions of years of scientific and technological
  evolution. That we don't see them is an interesting fact, not an
  "off-the-wall wild-assed guess".
  As somebody said, "In science, the silly question is often the
  first intimation of some totally new development." We can't be
  certain that such questions are irrelevant either to us or to
  our "visitors". You may feel certain, but that is just a wild-
  assed guess in my opinion.
  When we look around we find that the universe is ordered in
  certain interesting respects that we don't understand. In
  general, where does technology end and natural order begin? Can
  we even define a distinction that has universal meaning? What
  are the ultimate "limits to growth"? Ultimately, what _is_ the
  universe, and what is the true equilibrium state of a universe
  with intelligent agents in it?
  I think attempts to think clearly about difficult and subtle
  problems are always welcome. They're rare enough.

  Martin Shough

  I clearly understand a carrier versus modulation, having dealt
  with these concepts for many years.
  What I didn't understand is how a report of audio in the 200 to
  400 Hz range had anything to do with microwave audio. Or what
  source of a sufficiently powerful microwave signal might have
  been at the Fatima site in 1917.
  There is a little confusion from microwave audio effects, in
  that the beginning of the phenomenon was the hearing of a
  buzzing sound in the skulls of World War II radar technicians.
   The buzz is the result of individual pulses, one single pulse
  causing a single click.
  Voice is transmitted as a series of individual clicks, one click
  per zero axis crossing in a chosen direction. I.e. all crossings
  in a "downward" direction, or, all crossings in an "upward"
  direction, but not both. This is a primitive form of digital
  audio.
  My reply explaining that microwave hearing is not what is in use
  today was to show that far more sophisticated equipment exists
  now. In turn, my personal opinion only, such very advanced
  equipment supports the idea that UFO-related phenomena are now
  something more than just the vivid imaginations of "true
  believers." They are happening often to people far removed from
  UFO encounters.

  Eleanor White

Re: ETH Does Not Solve The Fermi Paradox - Chace

  >technological evolution. That we don't see them is an

  <snip>

  This is what I was getting at when I said that the ETH does not
  solve the Fermi Paradox. The way I've always heard the story
  told, Fermi asked the question because he had been thinking
  about models of interstellar migration. We know the average
  distances between stars, the approximate number of stars in the
  galaxy and so forth, so we can do some basic calculations if we
  make some assumptions about the speed of starships, the amount
  of time a new colony must develop before it can launch ships of
  its own, etc. Even if we use very conservative assumptions, such
  as limiting starship speeds to a small fraction of the speed of
  light and assuming many centuries must pass before a planet can
  start sending out its own colonists, these models predict that
  it should be possible for a single starfaring civilization to
  colonize the galaxy within a period of time of a few tens of
  millions of years. That's the blink of an eye compared to the
  age of the galaxy.
  Basically the only assumptions we are making with this model is
  that a hypothetical extraterrestrial civilization behaves like
  Europeans or Pacific Islanders (or any number of nonhuman
  species that have a pattern of expanding into new territory),
  and has access to technology on par with advanced nuclear
  rocketry (plus self-contained biospheres, good shielding and
  other technicalities). It is a conservative model, and it says
  that they should be here already. So where are they? Stanton
  Friedman would argue (and I agree) that we see their atmospheric
  excursion modules on a regular basis. But that doesn't entirely
  resolve the issue because we still don't know "the true
  equilibrium state of a universe with intelligent agents in it."
  Frank Drake believes that interstellar travel is so difficult
  and impractical that our galaxy's equilibrium state has pretty
  much all of the extraterrestrial civilizations staying at home,
  within the immediate environs of their own sun. If we're lucky
  and persistent, and fund the SETI program adequately, perhaps
  we'll be able to eavesdrop on the radio transmissions from some
  of those civilizations. Others have concluded that Drake and his
  SETI colleagues are being far too conservative, and interstellar
  migration should be feasible for a civilization only a little
  bit more advanced than our own. If you believe that, as I do,
  and if you also ignore the UFO phenomenon, then the colonization
  models pretty much force you to conclude that either they do not
  exist, or they are invisible to us, for some reason or other.
  As Cathy Reason stated, there are basically two stable
  equilibrium states: one in which they have colonized the whole
  galaxy, and the other in which they do not exist. To get another
  equilibrium state one has to make additional assumptions, such
  as the existence some terrible destructive force in the galaxy
  that sterilizes great swaths of galactic space every few million
  years. Afterwards those areas lie fallow until they can be re-
  colonized again. With the introduction of such a fudge factor
  one can have a galaxy that never gets completely colonized. The
  hypothetical destructive force could be an astronomical
  phenomenon such as supernova explosions, or maybe some factor
  inherent to galactic civilization such as interstellar war or a
  tendency to collapse and die out every so often (bad memes). But
  if we are following Occam's razor, we try to avoid making
  additional assumptions like that (although, honestly, we cannot
  rule them out either).
  There have been some thoughtful responses on the List about why
  the ETs might be effectively invisible to us. They may prefer to


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m05-012.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:16]
Re: ETH Does Not Solve The Fermi Paradox - Chace

  live in artificial space habitats, hollowed out asteroids,
  underground, under the sea, etc. My main problem with these
  ideas is that _some_ of them should still like to live on the
  surfaces of planets when those habitats are available. Life
  generally evolves to fill every (or almost every) available
  niche. If a civilization overlooks perfectly good habitats it is
  not maximizing its chances of survival. Even if they are not
  adapted for life on some particular planet, they could
  presumably remedy that situation with genetic engineering or
  some other adaptive technology. Also, the preponderance of
  humanoids among UFO occupant reports suggests to me that,
  ancestrally at least, these beings come from environments not
  too dissimilar from Earth's surface.
  Our ignorance of what technologies are possible, and the
  advantages and disadvantages associated with those technologies,
  is one of the main reasons why we are still stuck with the Fermi
  Paradox. Why doesn't civilization in our galaxy resemble the
  Galactic Republic from George Lucas's Star Wars films? Why
  aren't we fully conscious participants in some ancient galactic
  civilization, where technologies such as hyperspace travel and
  repulsor fields are taken for granted no matter what planet you
  live on? One reason is that the actual technologies that are
  possible or practical in the real world may be quite different
  from what is possible in the movies. But I don't think anyone
  really has the answers about that, in spite of claims by (to
  borrow a Friedmanism) fossilized physicists that they know
  faster than light travel or gravity manipulation is impossible,
  for example.
  What's going on in the galaxy? We are terribly ignorant of the
  history of technological civilization in the Milky Way galaxy.
  All we can say is that we see UFOs buzzing the countryside,
  occasionally showing off (or so it seems) over Arizona or
  Mexico, and sometimes landing so that the little humanoids on
  board can pick up some rocks, or do capture-release studies (or
  transgenics programs) on Earth's native wildlife (humans). Is
  this normal? I mean, galactically speaking? How long have ET
  civilizations been conducting surveillance of the Earth without
  actually colonizing it? Of course, Dr. David Jacobs might argue
  that the UFO abduction phenomenon is a process of colonization.
  But if so, why did they wait so long? Our planet has been
  habitable for about a billion years.
  This gets us back to the question of how much we know about
  Earth's deep past. I have a B.A. in biology, with a
  concentration in ecology, evolution and behavior, so that's
  where I'm coming from, education-wise. In college I took courses
  on paleontology, evolution, biogeography, etc. (I was always
  wondering what this perspective had to say about the
  distribution of extraterrestrial civilizations in the galaxy,
  the description of the ecological niches they occupy, etc.)
  Well, in spite of Young-Earth Creationism and so forth, we
  actually do know a great deal about our planet's deep past. We
  can use the geological and fossil records to put constraints on
  what may have happened long ago as far as past colonizations of
  our planet by extraterrestrial civilizations is concerned.
  If modern civilization is any example, we might expect a
  colonization event in the deep past to be associated with an
  otherwise unexplained mass extinction. Also, our modern global
  civilization has a terrible problem with alien species, by which
  I mean displaced terrestrial species such as tree snakes in Guam
  or rabbits in Australia. (Maybe the chupacabras is some ET's pet
  that got too big to take care of.) If we find evidence in the
  fossil record of animals from different parts of the world
  suddenly appearing in other parts of the world, in the absence
  of any independently verified land bridges or other natural
  means of making the journey, we might interpret that as evidence
  for the existence of a civilization at that time. However, I
  would argue based on what was known when I was in college (back
  in the early nineties) that there is not much evidence of this
  kind of thing. My understanding is that mysterious mass
  extinctions and "teleportations" of wildlife are even better
  understood today than they were then, with the independent
  evidence that has since been gathered of past asteroid impacts,
  continental drift, etc. So as far as the fossil record is
  concerned, I don't see much evidence that ET ever colonized our
  planet, at least not on the global scale we might expect if they
  behave anything like we do. Basically, I don't think Earth ever
  looked like the city world of Coruscant from Star Wars. That


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m05-012.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:16]
Re: ETH Does Not Solve The Fermi Paradox - Chace

  still doesn't rule out small, eco-friendly alien colonies,
  however. And that doesn't rule out past alien cities in caverns
  underground or on the sea floor. But the constraints imposed by
  Earth's geologic record tell us that extraterrestrial
  civilizations, for whatever reason, have (apparently) never had
  a global civilization on this planet like the one we have today.
  What does that mean? What does the ongoing UFO presence mean?
  What is the Earth to them, that they sample its environment and
  its life forms, but never appear to exploit it as fully as we
  might in their situation? Do they have some kind of symbiotic
  relationship with Earth's biosphere? If so, is symbiosis with
  earthlike planets a general characteristic of starfaring
  cultures in our galaxy? Are planets like Earth laboratories or
  pharmaceutical factories for ET civilizations? And just how many
  times has the deed to planet Earth exchanged hands over the past
  4.6 billion years?
  Whatever the solution to the aspects of the Fermi Paradox that
  are unresolved by the Extraterrestrial Hypothesis, it needs to
  be consistent with what we observe of UFOs and the appearance,
  behavior and technology of their occupants. It also needs to be
  consistent with the findings of paleontologists, geneticists,
  anthropologists, archeologists and all those who study the
  Earth's past. The Fermi Paradox still stands. The ETH only
  weakens it a bit.

  David W. Chace

  SECRECY NEWS
  from the FAS Project on Government Secrecy
  Volume 2006, Issue No. 2
  January 5, 2006

  **           STATE SECRETS: REVISITING U.S. V. REYNOLDS
  **           AN OPERATIONAL FILES EXEMPTION FOR DIA
  **           A MILLION FOR THE PUBLIC INTEREST DECLASS BOARD
  **           CRS ON NATIONAL SECURITY WHISTLEBLOWERS
  **           PUBLIC ACCESS TO WORLD LAW BULLETIN URGED

  STATE SECRETS: REVISITING U.S. V. REYNOLDS
  The 1953 Supreme Court ruling in United States v. Reynolds
  enshrined the "state secrets privilege" in U.S. jurisprudence,
  entitling the executive branch to withhold information about
  "military matters which, in the interest of national security,
  should not be divulged."
  "Yet United States v. Reynolds... rests on a lie," according to
  a petition filed with the Supreme Court last month.
  Fifty years ago, Air Force officials asserted under oath that
  documents at issue in the case contained state secrets
  pertaining to an Air Force plane that crashed, and refused to
  disclose them to the plaintiffs, widows of the fallen Air Force
  crew members.
  But a half century later, when the documents were eventually
  released, no such secrets concerning the plane's mission or
  onboard equipment were to be found.
  The petitioners, heirs to the original plaintiffs in Reynolds,
  are now asking the Supreme Court to review the case and to
  permit them to argue that they were defrauded by the government.
  The petitioners were rebuffed by the Court in 2003 when they
  first sought reconsideration of the 1953 ruling, and their
  arguments have subsequently been rejected by the lower courts as
  well.
  Still, the case raises interesting questions not only about the
  integrity of the original Reynolds decision, which is a
  cornerstone of national security law, but also about the
  judicial system's capacity to acknowledge and correct its
  errors.
  A copy of the Petition for a Writ of Certiorari in the case now
  captioned Herring v. U.S., filed at the Supreme Court on
  December 21, 2005 is posted here (252 pages, 500 kb):
  http://www.fas.org/sgp/jud/herring1205.pdf

  AN OPERATIONAL FILES EXEMPTION FOR DIA
  Congress granted the Defense Intelligence Agency an exemption


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m05-019.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:20]
Re: Secrecy News -- 01/05/06 - Aftergood

  from the Freedom of Information Act for its "operational files,"
  but only for the next two years.
  DIA is the fifth intelligence agency -- after CIA, NSA, NRO and
  NGA -- to receive such an exemption, which permits it to exclude
  from searching or reviewing for release under FOIA files "that
  document the conduct of foreign intelligence or
  counterintelligence operations."
  Opponents of the measure were concerned that the exemption could
  be used indiscriminately to withhold intelligence records that
  would otherwise be eligible for disclosure under FOIA.
  So it was a partial victory for critics when Congress imposed an
  unprecedented "sunset"on the exemption, such that it will be
  terminated at the end of December 2007.
  The final language of the provision, contained in the FY 2006
  Defense Authorization Act, and the accompanying report language,
  may be found here:
  http://www.fas.org/sgp/congress/2005/dia-opfiles.html

  A MILLION FOR THE PUBLIC INTEREST DECLASS BOARD
  Congress finally appropriated $1 million for the Public Interest
  Declassification Board (PIDB), a White House advisory body that
  has been dormant for the past five years. The money was
  allocated without comment in the final version of the FY 2006
  Defense Appropriations Act (H.R. 2863).
  For PIDB membership and related information, see:
  http://www.fas.org/sgp/congress/2005/pida.html

  CRS ON NATIONAL SECURITY WHISTLEBLOWERS
  The statutory framework that governs national security
  whistleblowers -- government employees who disclose malfeasance
  involving classified information or activities -- is examined in
  a new report from the Congressional Research Service.
  "Whistleblowers have helped uncover agency wrongdoing,
  illegalities, waste, and corruption," the 43 page CRS report
  finds.
  "The interest of Congress in maintaining an open channel with
  agency employees is demonstrated through such statutes as Lloyd-
  LaFollette, the appropriations riders on the nondisclosure
  policy, the Military Whistleblower Protection Act, and the
  Intelligence Community Whistleblower Act."
  See "National Security Whistleblowers," December 30, 2005:
  http://www.fas.org/sgp/crs/natsec/RL33215.pdf
  Political pressure is growing to provide improved protection for
  national security whistleblowers, who are often vulnerable to
  official retaliation.
  "Under today's failed protection regimen, whistleblowers are
  forced to go to the national news media which often does a
  better job of protecting their identities than the Congress
  does," said Danielle Brian, Executive Director of the Project On
  Government Oversight (POGO), which circulated the CRS report
  today.
  "National Security employees' highest duty is to the
  Constitution, and they should not have to sacrifice their
  careers or financial security in doing what is right," said
  Sibel Edmonds, president of the National Security Whistleblowers
  Coalition, which advocates stronger whistleblower protections.
  "A former National Security Agency official wants to tell
  Congress about electronic intelligence programs that he asserts
  were carried out illegally by the NSA and the Defense
  Intelligence Agency," writes Bill Gertz in the Washington Times
  today.

                                                        Nick Pope And The FSWP
  From: Joe McGonagle <joe.mcgonagle.nul>
  Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2006 22:45:46 +0000
  Fwd Date: Fri, 06 Jan 2006 11:16:52 -0500
  Subject: Nick Pope And The FSWP

  Hello Listers,
  Back in May last year, I wrote (during an on-List dialogue with
  Nick Pope):
  "I have tonight submitted a FoIA request which should
  definitively resolve the question. If it turns out that Georgina
  submitted her request before Clarke and Roberts circulated
  details of the discovery, I shall publicly apologise to her and
  you on-List. If it appears that the request was subsequent to
  C&R's announcement, I would hope that you would have the grace
  to do the same."
  The entire post can be viewed at:
  http://www.virtuallystrange.net/ufo/updates/2005/may/m25-023.shtml
  Well, the enquiry took two seperate requests to fulfil, and the
  results are now in.
  The _only_ correspondents with either/both the UFO desk and the
  Departmental Records Officer (DRO) at the MoD in relation to the
  FSWP were David Clarke and Andy Roberts during the period April
  2000 to April 2002. There is no question as to anyone having
  seen the report prior to April 2000, since there is only one
  copy (now) known to exist which was held by the MoD DRO. This
  was not discovered until David Clarke specifically asked the
  records officer to conduct a search for it. During May 2001, the
  DRO's staff found the report, and wrote the following to Clarke:
  "...during your exchanges of correspondence with DAS (Sec),
  formerly Sec(AS), in September/October last year [2000 - JM] a
  number of closed files, identified by you, were examined for
  DS/JTIC Report Number 7. Although unsuccessful my staff remained
  alert to your interest in this report. As a consequence of a
  routine re-review of another file (DEFE19/9 Scientific
  Intelligence 1948-1960) I am pleased to be able to advise that a
  surviving copy (Copy No 17) of Report No 7 has been found."
  Included with the letter was a copy of the report.
  Now there was only one copy of this document, which was under
  the control of the MoD DRO. Until it was released at the PRO in
  January 2002, any request for a copy would have had to pass via
  the DRO, and there were no other requests up to and including
  April 2002. In the meantime, Clarke released information about
  the report to the press and a story was published in "The
  Observer" on 21st October 2001 see:
  http://observer.guardian.co.uk/uk_news/story/0,,577850,00.html
  On the same date, Clarke and Roberts placed scans of the
  documents on their website (www.flyingsaucery.com) and notified
  this List of their discovery and the URL, see:
  http://www.virtuallystrange.net/ufo/updates/2001/oct/m21-004.shtml
  Up until 21st October 2001, no-one other than Clarke and Roberts
  knew that the report had been found, or what it contained.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-002.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:22]
Nick Pope And The FSWP


  In January 2002, Nick Pope wrote in his "Weird World" column for
  Bruni's "Hot Gossip" magazine:
  "Hard on the heels of Georgina Bruni's scoop concerning the
  release of MOD documents on the Rendlesham Forest incident, two
  enterprising members of the public have stumbled upon 'DSI/JTIC
  Report No. 7'."
  See:
  http://www.virtuallystrange.net/ufo/updates/2002/jan/m03-019.shtml
  Note that there is no mention by name of Clarke or Roberts, and
  they are described as having "stumbled upon" the report. There
  is also no mention of Bruni or Popehaving discovered the
  document. Having read the extensive correspondence between the
  MoD and Clarke/Roberts, the report was not simply "stumbled
  upon", but was uncovered through dilligent, persistent and
  dedicated research.
  The following April (2002) an article focussed on the FSWP co-
  authored by Georgina Bruni and Nick Pope appeared in the UK UFO
  Magazine, claiming a "World Exclusive", and not mentioning
  either Clarke or Roberts.
  Since then, Pope and Bruni have been given every possible
  opportunity to set the record straight, but they have
  dogmatically refused to acknowledge the true provenance of the
  FSWP. In May last year, I asked Pope:
  "Please can you elaborate on exactly how and when you became
  aware of the FSWP document and the date that you requested a
  copy of it?"
  to which he replied:
  "Georgina Bruni obtained them in 2001, but I don't know
  precisely when. She learned of their existence through unrelated
  research into the Cold War. I didn't find out that she had the
  papers until later...
  ...Clarke and Roberts were sent the documents by the MOD, as
  were numerous other ufologists and journalists."
  see: http://www.virtuallystrange.net/ufo/updates/2005/may/m24-007.shtml
  Insinuating that Bruni had either discovered the report prior to
  C&R, or that she was oblivious to their efforts and "discovered"
  it after they did independently - both scenarios are clearly
  untenable. Additionally, no-one other than C&R was sent copies
  of the report by the MoD before April 2002.
  A few days later in a response to Martin Shough on-list at:
  http://www.virtuallystrange.net/ufo/updates/2005/may/m26-009.shtml
  Pope wrote:
  "My understanding is that several people acquired them in 2001.
  Georgina Bruni, Dave Clarke and Andy Roberts definitely did. I
  believe that several others did too, but I'm certainly not able
  to give a definitive list of who got what document on what date.
  I'll have to leave that to those concerned."
  Now, is Pope innocent and misinformed, or is he more devious
  than that? Clearly all of the evidence shows that Bruni could
  not have seen a copy of the report before it's publication at
  www.flyingsaucery.com in October 2001. Furthermore, she did not
  obtain a copy from the MoD before April 2002, and must have
  obtained her copy from the PRO in January 2002 at the earliest.
  Pope then goes on to write:
  "I don't dispute that Clarke and Roberts were the first
  ufologists to _claim_ that they obtained the documents. They've
  _claimed_ to be the first to acquire all sorts of material; an
  article in The Observer on May 5 2002 implied they uncovered a
  CIA memo on UFOs written by Walter B. Smith, when in fact it was
  published by Timothy Good in 1987, in his book Above Top Secret.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-002.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:22]
Nick Pope And The FSWP

  Frankly, I've given up believing a word that Clarke and Roberts
  say."
  This saga reveals a lot about their integrity and character, and
  raises questions about the reliability of their other claims....

  Regards,
  Joe

                                        Re: ETH Does Not Solve The Fermi Paradox -
  From: Joe McGonagle <joe.mcgonagle.nul>
  Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2006 20:44:29 +0000
  Fwd Date: Fri, 06 Jan 2006 11:08:48 -0500
  Subject: Re: ETH Does Not Solve The Fermi Paradox -

  Hello List,
  I shan't attempt to answer all of the various posts point by
  point - it is ironic that my comments have provoked even more of
  what I described as a waste of bandwidth!
  In response to Cathy and Martin, I think you are mistaken about
  the two options for a stable state. Illogical though it might
  sound, I think that chaos is a third stable state!
  Although there may appear to be stability when viewed over an
  extremely long time period (Millions of Millions of years), when
  examined in smaller but at least for humanity, very significant
  time periods (in the order of say a hundred thousand years),
  parts of the universe are in a state of flux.
  There are so many variable factors when history and the
  development of the universe is observed in relatively short
  timescale that it is highly unlikely in my view that similar (in
  terms of development) species evolve in the same general area of
  space within, say, 100,000 years of each other. If that is so,
  any species that have evolved into intelligent life-forms have
  most probably had at least double the evolutionary life that we
  humans have had so far (if they are not at the Chimpanzee or
  equivalent stage still). They (and their technology, culture,
  morals, etc) would be as unrecognisable to us as our values and
  technology are to chimpanzees.
  Any ET intelligence does not only have the advantage of longer
  evolution, but will almost certainly have a completely different
  evolutionary path to our own. Putting that into a terrestrial
  context, trying to predict the behaviour and motivation of any
  ET intelligence is akin to a Coelacanth attempting to predict
  human behaviour and values. All that we can do is speculate, but
  we have little (if any) information on which to base such
  speculation of ET technology, culture, morals, etc. IMO it was
  extremely premature of Fermi to speculate based on so little
  data, and his so-called paradox is not worth the databytes on
  the WWW (just as my own speculative comments above are of little
  value!).

  Cheers,
  Joe

  typically in the order of several hundred Hz - the bee-buzz. The
  radar transmitter is silent for almost all of the time,
  occasionally emitting the very short sharp pulses you mention,
  each a burst of the carrier frequency (say MHz of GHz), at a
  pulse-modulated frequency of a few hundred Hz. This is what a
  bee-buzz has to do with microwave audio. OK?

  from the FAS Project on Government Secrecy
  Volume 2006, Issue No. 3
  January 6, 2006

  **           CRS ON WARRANTLESS SURVEILLANCE
  **           INFORMATION SHARING POLICY FAULTED
  **           KEEPING CURRENT ON GOVERNMENT SECRECY

  CRS ON WARRANTLESS SURVEILLANCE
  The Congressional Research Service has prepared a detailed
  evaluation of Bush Administration legal claims regarding
  Presidential authority to conduct warrantless electronic
  surveillance within the United States.
  The CRS authors sift through each of the statutory,
  constitutional and other arguments that have been presented in
  defense of the reported NSA surveillance activity, and
  ultimately find them wanting.
  A final determination on the matter is impossible, they note,
  "without an understanding of the specific facts involved and the
  nature of the President's authorization, which are for the most
  part classified."
  In the end, however, "the Administration's legal justification,
  as presented in the [December 22, 2005] summary analysis from
  the Office of Legislative Affairs, does not seem to be as well-
  grounded as the tenor of that letter suggests," they cautiously
  conclude.
  See "Presidential Authority to Conduct Warrantless Electronic
  Surveillance to Gather Foreign Intelligence Information,"
  Congressional Research Service, January 5, 2006:
  http://www.fas.org/sgp/crs/intel/m010506.pdf

  INFORMATION SHARING POLICY FAULTED
  Government initiatives to promote information sharing among and
  between federal and state agencies have failed to achieve their
  objectives, a new congressional staff report finds.
  "Despite numerous directives, exhortations, and invitations to
  do so, federal policymakers have failed to develop uniform
  standards for converting classified intelligence into an
  unclassified or 'less classified' format that can be
  disseminated rapidly to appropriate state, local, and tribal
  authorities to thwart terrorist attacks," the report says.
  The reports recounts in unblinking detail each new announcement
  of a bold innovation in information sharing policy, and its
  subsequent failure.
  "This distressing lack of leadership has persisted for more than


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-011.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:26]
Secrecy News -- 01/06/06

  four years."
  The authors propose a law enforcement-driven approach to
  information sharing based on a model adopted in the United
  Kingdom.
  The report was prepared by Democratic staff for Rep. Bennie G.
  Thompson, ranking member of the House Committee on Homeland
  Security.
  See "Beyond Connecting the Dots: A VITAL Framework for Sharing
  Law Enforcement Intelligence Information," House Committee on
  Homeland Security Democratic Staff Report, December 28, 2005:
  http://www.fas.org/irp/congress/2005_rpt/vital.pdf

  KEEPING CURRENT ON GOVERNMENT SECRECY
  A sizable inventory of organizations, web sites, and
  publications concerned in some way with government secrecy was
  presented in a recent survey.
  "In the interest of sharing information, here is a list of Web
  sites, blogs, listservs, and newsletters that could help clients
  needing access to government documents but who might experience
  difficulty locating that information. The list is arranged by
  government watchdog sites, sites that provide access to
  government documents, sites that document government secrecy,
  and advocacy groups that report on FOIA news."
  See "Shhh!!: Keeping Current on Government Secrecy" by Laura
  Gordon-Murnane, Searcher: The Magazine for Database
  Professionals, January 2006:
  http://www.infotoday.com/searcher/jan06/Gordon-Murnane.shtml

                                                   Warp Drive Is Closer To Reality
  From: Steven Kaeser <steve.nul>
  Date: Fri, 06 Jan 2006 09:41:56 -0500
  Fwd Date: Fri, 06 Jan 2006 13:43:24 -0500
  Subject: Warp Drive Is Closer To Reality

  MSS VX News: [Scotsman] Warp Drive Being Built -- Welcome to
  Mars express: only a three hour trip [Jan 5 2006]
  Welcome to Mars express: only a three hour trip
  IAN JOHNSTON SCIENCE CORRESPONDENT
  AN EXTRAORDINARY "hyperspace" engine that could make
  interstellar space travel a reality by flying into other
  dimensions is being investigated by the United States
  government.
  The hypothetical device, which has been outlined in principle
  but is based on a controversial theory about the fabric of the
  universe, could potentially allow a spacecraft to travel to Mars
  in three hours and journey to a star 11 light years away in just
  80 days, according to a report in today's New Scientist
  magazine.
  The theoretical engine works by creating an intense magnetic
  field that, according to ideas first developed by the late
  scientist Burkhard Heim in the 1950s, would produce a
  gravitational field and result in thrust for a spacecraft.
  Also, if a large enough magnetic field was created, the craft
  would slip into a different dimension, where the speed of light
  is faster, allowing incredible speeds to be reached. Switching
  off the magnetic field would result in the engine reappearing in
  our current dimension.
  The US air force has expressed an interest in the idea and
  scientists working for the American Department of Energy - which
  has a device known as the Z Machine that could generate the kind
  of magnetic fields required to drive the engine - say they may
  carry out a test if the theory withstands further scrutiny.
  Professor Jochem Hauser, one of the scientists who put forward
  the idea, told The Scotsman that if everything went well a
  working engine could be tested in about five years.
  However, Prof Hauser, a physicist at the Applied Sciences
  University in Salzgitter, Germany, and a former chief of
  aerodynamics at the European Space Agency, cautioned it was
  based on a highly controversial theory that would require a
  significant change in the current understanding of the laws of
  physics.
  "It would be amazing. I have been working on propulsion systems
  for quite a while and it would be the most amazing thing. The
  benefits would be almost unlimited," he said.
  "But this thing is not around the corner; we first have to prove
  the basic science is correct and there are quite a few
  physicists who have a different opinion.
  "It's our job to prove we are right and we are working on that."
  He said the engine would enable spaceships to travel to
  different solar systems. "If the theory is correct then this is


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-013.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:27]
Warp Drive Is Closer To Reality

  not science fiction, it is science fact," Prof Hauser said.
  "NASA have contacted me and next week I'm going to see someone
  from the [US] air force to talk about it further, but it is at a
  very early stage. I think the best-case scenario would be within
  the next five years [to build a test device] if the technology
  works."
  The US authorities' attention was attracted after Prof Hauser
  and an Austrian colleague, Walter Droscher, wrote a paper called
  "Guidelines for a space propulsion device based on Heim's
  quantum theory".

  Take a leap into hyperspace
          * 05 January 2006
          * NewScientist.com news service
          * Haiko Lietz
  http://www.newscientist.com/channel/fundamentals/mg18925331.200.html
  EVERY year, the American Institute of Aeronautics and
  Astronautics awards prizes for the best papers presented at its
  annual conference. Last year's winner in the nuclear and future
  flight category went to a paper calling for experimental tests
  of an astonishing new type of engine. According to the paper,
  this hyperdrive motor would propel a craft through another
  dimension at enormous speeds. It could leave Earth at lunchtime
  and get to the moon in time for dinner. There's just one catch:
  the idea relies on an obscure and largely unrecognised kind of
  physics. Can they possibly be serious?
  The AIAA is certainly not embarrassed. What's more, the US
  military has begun to cast its eyes over the hyperdrive concept,
  and a space propulsion researcher at the US Department of
  Energy's Sandia National Laboratories has said he would be
  interested in putting the idea to the test. And despite the
  bafflement of most physicists at the theory that supposedly
  underpins it, Pavlos Mikellides, an aerospace engineer at the
  Arizona State University in Tempe who reviewed the winning
  paper, stands by the committee's choice. "Even though such
  features have been explored before, this particular approach is
  quite unique," he says.
  Unique it certainly is. If the experiment gets the go-ahead and
  works, it could reveal new interactions between the fundamental
  forces of nature that would change the future of space travel.
  Forget spending six months or more holed up in a rocket on the
  way to Mars, a round trip on the hyperdrive could take as little
  as 5 hours. All our worries about astronauts' muscles wasting
  away or their DNA being irreparably damaged by cosmic radiation
  would disappear overnight. What's more the device would put
  travel to the stars within reach for the first time.
  But can the hyperdrive really get off the ground?
  The answer to that question hinges on the work of a little-known
  German physicist. Burkhard Heim began to explore the hyperdrive
  propulsion concept in the 1950s as a spin-off from his attempts
  to heal the biggest divide in physics: the rift between quantum
  mechanics and Einstein's general theory of relativity.
  Quantum theory describes the realm of the very small - atoms,
  electrons and elementary particles - while general relativity
  deals with gravity. The two theories are immensely successful in
  their separate spheres. The clash arises when it comes to
  describing the basic structure of space. In general relativity,
  space-time is an active, malleable fabric. It has four
  dimensions - three of space and one of time - that deform when
  masses are placed in them. In Einstein's formulation, the force
  of gravity is a result of the deformation of these dimensions.
  Quantum theory, on the other hand, demands that space is a fixed
  and passive stage, something simply there for particles to exist
  on. It also suggests that space itself must somehow be made up
  of discrete, quantum elements.
  In the early 1950s, Heim began to rewrite the equations of
  general relativity in a quantum framework. He drew on Einstein's
  idea that the gravitational force emerges from the dimensions of


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-013.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:27]
Warp Drive Is Closer To Reality

  space and time, but suggested that all fundamental forces,
  including electromagnetism, might emerge from a new, different
  set of dimensions. Originally he had four extra dimensions, but
  he discarded two of them believing that they did not produce any
  forces, and settled for adding a new two-dimensional "sub-space"
  onto Einstein's four-dimensional space-time.
  In Heim's six-dimensional world, the forces of gravity and
  electromagnetism are coupled together. Even in our familiar
  four-dimensional world, we can see a link between the two forces
  through the behaviour of fundamental particles such as the
  electron. An electron has both mass and charge. When an electron
  falls under the pull of gravity its moving electric charge
  creates a magnetic field. And if you use an electromagnetic
  field to accelerate an electron you move the gravitational field
  associated with its mass. But in the four dimensions we know,
  you cannot change the strength of gravity simply by cranking up
  the electromagnetic field.
  In Heim's view of space and time, this limitation disappears. He
  claimed it is possible to convert electromagnetic energy into
  gravitational and back again, and speculated that a rotating
  magnetic field could reduce the influence of gravity on a
  spacecraft enough for it to take off.
  When he presented his idea in public in 1957, he became an
  instant celebrity. Wernher von Braun, the German engineer who at
  the time was leading the Saturn rocket programme that later
  launched astronauts to the moon, approached Heim about his work
  and asked whether the expensive Saturn rockets were worthwhile.
  And in a letter in 1964, the German relativity theorist Pascual
  Jordan, who had worked with the distinguished physicists Max
  Born and Werner Heisenberg and was a member of the Nobel
  committee, told Heim that his plan was so important "that its
  successful experimental treatment would without doubt make the
  researcher a candidate for the Nobel prize".
  But all this attention only led Heim to retreat from the public
  eye. This was partly because of his severe multiple
  disabilities, caused by a lab accident when he was still in his
  teens. But Heim was also reluctant to disclose his theory
  without an experiment to prove it. He never learned English
  because he did not want his work to leave the country. As a
  result, very few people knew about his work and no one came up
  with the necessary research funding. In 1958 the aerospace
  company B=F6lkow did offer some money, but not enough to do the
  proposed experiment.
  While Heim waited for more money to come in, the company's
  director, Ludwig B=F6lkow, encouraged him to develop his theory
  further. Heim took his advice, and one of the results was a
  theorem that led to a series of formulae for calculating the
  masses of the fundamental particles - something conventional
  theories have conspicuously failed to achieve. He outlined this
  work in 1977 in the Max Planck Institute's journal Zeitschrift
  f=FCr Naturforschung, his only peer-reviewed paper. In an abstruse
  way that few physicists even claim to understand, the formulae
  work out a particle's mass starting from physical
  characteristics, such as its charge and angular momentum.
  Yet the theorem has proved surprisingly powerful. The standard
  model of physics, which is generally accepted as the best
  available theory of elementary particles, is incapable of
  predicting a particle's mass. Even the accepted means of
  estimating mass theoretically, known as lattice quantum
  chromodynamics, only gets to between 1 and 10 per cent of the
  experimental values.

  Gravity reduction
  But in 1982, when researchers at the German Electron Synchrotron
  (DESY) in Hamburg implemented Heim's mass theorem in a computer
  program, it predicted masses of fundamental particles that
  matched the measured values to within the accuracy of
  experimental error. If they are let down by anything, it is the
  precision to which we know the values of the fundamental
  constants. Two years after Heim's death in 2001, his long-term
  collaborator Illobrand von Ludwiger calculated the mass formula
  using a more accurate gravitational constant. "The masses came
  out even more precise," he says.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-013.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:27]
Warp Drive Is Closer To Reality


  After publishing the mass formulae, Heim never really looked at
  hyperspace propulsion again. Instead, in response to requests
  for more information about the theory behind the mass
  predictions, he spent all his time detailing his ideas in three
  books published in German. It was only in 1980, when the first
  of his books came to the attention of a retired Austrian patent
  officer called Walter Dr=F6scher, that the hyperspace propulsion
  idea came back to life. Dr=F6scher looked again at Heim's ideas
  and produced an "extended" version, resurrecting the dimensions
  that Heim originally discarded. The result is "Heim-Dr=F6scher
  space", a mathematical description of an eight-dimensional
  universe.
   From this, Dr=F6scher claims, you can derive the four forces
  known in physics: the gravitational and electromagnetic forces,
  and the strong and weak nuclear forces. But there's more to it
  than that. "If Heim's picture is to make sense," Dr=F6scher says,
  "we are forced to postulate two more fundamental forces." These
  are, Dr=F6scher claims, related to the familiar gravitational
  force: one is a repulsive anti-gravity similar to the dark
  energy that appears to be causing the universe's expansion to
  accelerate. And the other might be used to accelerate a
  spacecraft without any rocket fuel.
  This force is a result of the interaction of Heim's fifth and
  sixth dimensions and the extra dimensions that Dr=F6scher
  introduced. It produces pairs of "gravitophotons", particles
  that mediate the interconversion of electromagnetic and
  gravitational energy. Dr=F6scher teamed up with Jochem H=E4user, a
  physicist and professor of computer science at the University of
  Applied Sciences in Salzgitter, Germany, to turn the theoretical
  framework into a proposal for an experimental test. The paper
  they produced, "Guidelines for a space propulsion device based
  on Heim's quantum theory", is what won the AIAA's award last
  year.
  Claims of the possibility of "gravity reduction" or "anti-
  gravity" induced by magnetic fields have been investigated by
  NASA before (New Scientist, 12 January 2002, p 24). But this
  one, Dr=F6scher insists, is different. "Our theory is not about
  anti-gravity. It's about completely new fields with new
  properties," he says. And he and H=E4user have suggested an
  experiment to prove it.
  This will require a huge rotating ring placed above a
  superconducting coil to create an intense magnetic field. With a
  large enough current in the coil, and a large enough magnetic
  field, Dr=F6scher claims the electromagnetic force can reduce the
  gravitational pull on the ring to the point where it floats
  free. Dr=F6scher and H=E4user say that to completely counter Earth's
  pull on a 150-tonne spacecraft a magnetic field of around 25
  tesla would be needed. While that's 500,000 times the strength
  of Earth's magnetic field, pulsed magnets briefly reach field
  strengths up to 80 tesla. And Dr=F6scher and H=E4user go further.
  With a faster-spinning ring and an even stronger magnetic field,
  gravitophotons would interact with conventional gravity to
  produce a repulsive anti-gravity force, they suggest.
  Dr=F6scher is hazy about the details, but he suggests that a
  spacecraft fitted with a coil and ring could be propelled into a
  multidimensional hyperspace. Here the constants of nature could
  be different, and even the speed of light could be several times
  faster than we experience. If this happens, it would be possible
  to reach Mars in less than 3 hours and a star 11 light years
  away in only 80 days, Dr=F6scher and H=E4user say.
  So is this all fanciful nonsense, or a revolution in the making?
  The majority of physicists have never heard of Heim theory, and
  most of those contacted by New Scientist said they couldn't make
  sense of Dr=F6scher and H=E4user's description of the theory behind
  their proposed experiment. Following Heim theory is hard work
  even without Dr=F6scher's extension, says Markus P=F6ssel, a
  theoretical physicist at the Max Planck Institute for
  Gravitational Physics in Potsdam, Germany. Several years ago,
  while an undergraduate at the University of Hamburg, he took a
  careful look at Heim theory. He says he finds it "largely
  incomprehensible", and difficult to tie in with today's physics.
  "What is needed is a step-by-step introduction, beginning at
  modern physical concepts," he says.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-013.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:27]
Warp Drive Is Closer To Reality

  The general consensus seems to be that Dr=F6scher and H=E4user's
  theory is incomplete at best, and certainly extremely difficult
  to follow. And it has not passed any normal form of peer review,
  a fact that surprised the AIAA prize reviewers when they made
  their decision. "It seemed to be quite developed and ready for
  such publication," Mikellides told New Scientist.
  At the moment, the main reason for taking the proposal seriously
  must be Heim theory's uncannily successful prediction of
  particle masses. Maybe, just maybe, Heim theory really does have
  something to contribute to modern physics. "As far as I
  understand it, Heim theory is ingenious," says Hans Theodor
  Auerbach, a theoretical physicist at the Swiss Federal Institute
  of Technology in Zurich who worked with Heim. "I think that
  physics will take this direction in the future."
  It may be a long while before we find out if he's right. In its
  present design, Dr=F6scher and H=E4user's experiment requires a
  magnetic coil several metres in diameter capable of sustaining
  an enormous current density. Most engineers say that this is not
  feasible with existing materials and technology, but Roger
  Lenard, a space propulsion researcher at Sandia National
  Laboratories in New Mexico thinks it might just be possible.
  Sandia runs an X-ray generator known as the Z machine which
  "could probably generate the necessary field intensities and
  gradients".
  For now, though, Lenard considers the theory too shaky to
  justify the use of the Z machine. "I would be very interested in
  getting Sandia interested if we could get a more perspicacious
  introduction to the mathematics behind the proposed experiment,"
  he says. "Even if the results are negative, that, in my mind, is
  a successful experiment."

  Who was Burkhard Heim?
  Burkhard Heim had a remarkable life. Born in 1925 in Potsdam,
  Germany, he decided at the age of 6 that he wanted to become a
  rocket scientist. He disguised his designs in code so that no
  one could discover his secret. And in the cellar of his parents'
  house, he experimented with high explosives. But this was to
  lead to disaster.
  Towards the end of the second world war, he worked as an
  explosives developer, and an accident in 1944 in which a device
  exploded in his hands left him permanently disabled. He lost
  both his forearms, along with 90 per cent of his hearing and
  eyesight.
  After the war, he attended university in G=F6ttingen to study
  physics. The idea of propelling a spacecraft using quantum
  mechanics rather than rocket fuel led him to study general
  relativity and quantum mechanics. It took an enormous effort.
  =46rom 1948, his father and wife replaced his senses, spending
  hours reading papers and transcribing his calculations onto
  paper. And he developed a photographic memory.
  Supporters of Heim theory claim that it is a panacea for the
  troubles in modern physics. They say it unites quantum mechanics
  and general relativity, can predict the masses of the building
  blocks of matter from first principles, and can even explain the
  state of the universe 13.7 billion years ago.

  Source: The Lincolnshire Echo

  05 January 2006

  Are Aliens Watching Us?
  Spooked residents claim to have seen alien spaceships hovering
  over Lincolnshire.
  Two groups of people, who have all denied being under the
  influence of alcohol or drugs, said they saw the UFOs on
  December 30 and 31.
  They both claim that glowing objects hovered over them for a few
  seconds and then silently disappeared.
  No official radar records exist for the dates in question as RAF
  Waddington's air traffic control centre was closed.
  And the police say that they have received no reports of other
  sightings.
  But Beth Clarkson (58), of Dene Close, Skellingthorpe, is
  convinced that she saw a UFO. She was at a caravan convention at
  the Memorial Hall in Wellingore when it happened.
  "It was about 5pm on Saturday. I was fetching some water for the
  van with another man when he just gasped and pointed to the sky.
  There was this orange cone shaped object burning in the sky. It
  hovered for a while and then headed off towards Waddington.
  There was no sound, it was really eerie."
  Mum Sandy Gregory of St Peter's Avenue, Boultham, Lincoln, had a
  similar experience the next day.
  "My family and neighbours were stood out front at about midday
  and the strangest thing flew past at about tree height. It was
  like a plate with a flame on it and it was going at about
  20mph," she said. "Then it flew over Boultham Park and went
  towards the city. We don't know what it was - and no we weren't
  drunk."
  In May last year the Echo used the Freedom of Information Act to
  access information on UFO sightings across the county.
  Documents revealed that six unidentified flying objects had been
  reported in Lincolnshire's skies over the past five years.
  Flight Lieutenant Roger Steel, who works in air traffic control
  at RAF Waddington, said: "We only started operating the radar
  again yesterday and it was out of action from December 21 for
  Christmas so we have no records to check whether we picked
  anything up or not. "There are a number of possible conventional
  explanations.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m06-014.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:28]
Are Aliens Watching Us?


  "Obviously it could be aircraft. Since the opening of the new
  Robin Hood airport there's been a lot more activity. And there
  is also the possibility of the Humberside Police helicopter.
  This uses a powerful search light that creates a column of
  light. And the sound of the helicopter can often be blown away
  if there is a stiff breeze."
  Lincolnshire Police spokesman Tony Diggins said the force had
  received no UFO sighting reports over the festive season. "And
  to our knowledge the Humberside chopper was not out."
  In the know
  Under the Freedom of Information Act the Echo received details
  of all official UFO sightings reported to the military over the
  past five years.
  The records show six sightings involving seven objects reported
  to personnel in the county.
  All of the sightings were made by residents or motorists who
  claimed to have seen unexplained objects.
  But no reports explaining the sightings or showing the results
  of further investigations into their authenticity have been
  released.
  The sightings include reports of objects shaped like triangles,
  torpedoes or even cylinders. Others were recorded as "glowing"
  and "lights" in the night sky.
  The objects were reported to hover in the air, move silently,
  race across the sky and even spin. One "speeding light" was said
  to have "turned 180 degrees back on itself instantaneously".
  Another was reported to have hovered in the air before it "shot
  off creating a blue and white light some 30ft long".
  In November 2001 a resident of Gonerby, Grantham, reported that
  his house had started to shake and had experienced a power cut
  when a "glowing object" appeared over it.
  MoD records report the caller seeing what "looked like a
  missile" moving very fast.
  "Caller believes it could not have been an aircraft as it did
  not have wings," read the report.
  At the time the RAF reported no flights in the area.

  Hello Dick
  I feel that you are over-reacting against discussion of the so-
  called Fermi Paradox because of the way that it has been
  thoughtlessly invoked by idiots as a "proof" that there can't be
  any UFOs. Whatever Fermi may personally have thought, such
  circular thinking is indeed "baloney" and very irritating. But
  conversely, to say "Look, here _are_ these UFOs, so therefore
  Fermi's Paradox must be baloney" is, well, baloney. Fermi's
  Paradox survives all the baloney because, properly formulated,
  it appeals over the heads of these arguments to something more
  general.
  I understand why people may want to scream "We can't know
  anything about alien life! Anything is possible! We [present


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/jan/m07-001.shtml[10/12/2011 10:15:29]
Re: ETH Does Not Solve The Fermi Paradox - Shough

  company excepted] are mere primitive slime!" But I don't think
  we can be happy with this, even though the usual hide-bound
  debunker alternative is less attractive still. We have to try
  and find ways to make connections with the rest of science and
  find contexts where UFO observations might eventually have some
  evidential power. The recent Maccabee et al. inflation paper is
  an illustration. The cosmos is already looking like a very
  different place from the one in which the old battle between the
  Markowiczs and Keyhoes was fought with rockets and
  interplanetary travel times - and the night is yet young!
  We look out at the cosmos and we observe that it is not (to all
  appearances) transformed by technological activity. Other than
  our own activity, this appears to be true on all scales of
  nature: The surface of the earth, the solar system, the stellar
  neighbourhood, the em background, the galaxy, the local cluster,
  supercluster complexes, right up to the smooth CMB. That this is
  what astrophysicists and cosmologists see, when they look up, is
  a simple fact, not at all hard to verify by anyone, and
  perfectly falsifiable - by observing something different.
  Now of course people - some of them astrophysicists even - do
  experience things which lead us to question the meaning of this
  observation. One of these things is the UFO phenomenon here in
  our local cultural environment. UFOs might be held to falsify
  certain _inferences_ that people make from Fermi's Paradox, but
  they do not falsify the observation that underpins it: The
  cosmos does not, as far as we can see, appear to be transformed
  on any scale by technological activity other than our own.
  Fermi's so-called Paradox is similar to Olbers' so-called
  Paradox, repopularised by Bondi in the 1950s (about the same
  time) in the context of the big bang v. steady state debate: The
  night sky is dark and cold. Why, when it could be bright and
  hot?
  Whilst the angular area of any given stellar surface decreases as
  the square of the distance, the number of stellar surfaces
  potentially increases as the square of the distance, so there
  needs to be a good reason why the night sky is not uniformly as
  bright as the surface of the sun. General relativity supplies one
  solution: the universe is young and growing, and not infinite and
  eternal. Thermal inequilibrium implies cosmic time.
  Or you can look at it the other way around: Why are there any
  stars at all instead of just a uniform heat bath smoothing out
  the temperature gradient of thousands of K between the stars and
  the space between? However you look at it this is a question of
  thermodynamic equilibrium : We observe that this universe is far
  from the statistically-most-likely state of a universe selected
  at random from a notional ensemble of universes, and far from
  its own most stable state.
  These are profound reflections because they seem to associate
  the existence of conscious observers with a complex dynamical
  system in what we conceive to be a highly improbable state.
  Fermi's Paradox is possibly equally profound. As it is in the
  nature of stars to use gravitational negentropy to process light
  elements into radiation, so it is in the nature of life to
  metabolise entropy into local order and expand to colonise
  available niches. Fungi, bacteria and humans colonise. This is a
  general property not a specific one: living systems process
  energy into multiplying complexity as long as the energy is
  available and there is an ecospace for them to move into. Our
  accelerating technological culture seems to be an expression of
  a fundamental property of far-from-equilibrium systems. So, as
  we need an explanation of why the universe does not appear to be
  in thermal equilibrium, we may also need an explanation of why
  it is not in technological equilibrium.
  This is an "obvious" non-problem to the baloney-sellers: "Well
  they are the same issue aren't they? The universe is young and
  physics proves that rockets can't reach the speed of light
  etc.etc." (you know the script) so no technological culture has
  had time to metabolise and transform more than its own invisible
  tiny corner of the cosmos. But it's far from simple as soon as
  we start to think about what a universe in technological
  equilibrium is, and how we would recognise it, because obviously
  all properties of a universe completely transformed by
  technology would have been selected for, in the process of

  transformation. And that may includes us, as well as an
  unknowable proportion (up to 100%) of the physics in which we
  find that our existence is implicit.
  So maybe this is one extreme answer to our "paradox": We deny
  that we can truly tell the difference between the two
  equilibrium solutions of the Fermi Paradox because a universe
  devoid of technology is indistinguishable, a priori, from a
  universe totally saturated and transformed by technology -
   except that technological transformation is a way of
  understanding the gravitational negentropy that powers cosmic
  dynamics. Thus, maybe the universe _has_ been driven to a
  technological equilibrium, and one consequence of this is the
  thermodynamically far-from-equilibrium state giving rise to
  complex structure from supercluster complexes down to particle
  interactions, and us.
  Another way of looking at it would be to see this as an
  alternative to an anthropic point of view. The anthropic view
  says that only universes which are not driven to thermodynamic
  equilibrium are interesting enough to contain complex
  technological cultures, so it is inevitable that we find
  ourselves in such a far-from-equilibrium universe. There's an
  inescapable circular logic to this. But physicists don't
  traditionally like anthropic arguments, and the technological
  equilibrium hypothesis looks like a possible way of avoiding
  this one.
  (In terms of the various current elaborations of the Standard
  Cosmological Model, both approaches would imply a multiverse, in
  order to provide a meaningful state-space for "selection". I
  don't necessarily subscribe to this myself, but that's another
  story.)
  I could go on, but you may say, To hell with all this, give me
  the simple fact that there are UFOs flying around which directly
  proves ETH and short-circuits all this "swagging". But the UFO
  phenomenon isn't a simple fact is it? It is a complex,
  bewildering set of internally inconsistent facts almost none of
  which is unambiguously understood. True, if we cut and trim
  until we have removed from this mess everything but the reports
  of "craft" we can make a case that we are being visited by your
  "random explorers" and "atom-bomb explosion investigators".
  OK then, let's say we try and live with this "fact". The ET
  culture(s) responsible are then not so advanced technically that
  they have been able to saturate the cosmos at large or
  manipulate galactic mass-energy on a detectable scale or
  anything like this. They are organic creatures exploring and
  investigating the earth by means of aerospace technology that we
  can almost begin to speculate about. Their impact on the
  universe appears not much different from ours. We can relate to
  them. They are not gods. They are cosmic primitives, like we
  are.
  But this is where the difference between stable and unstable
  solutions comes in. We are proposing a state of almost-zero
  technological transformation, which almost, but _not_quite_,
  satisfies one extremum solution of the Fermi Paradox. The cosmos
  is very, very nearly empty of intelligence after 13.7 billion
  years. But not quite.
  Now it is possible that we are unique and special and that no
  other intelligent technological culture would ever have expanded
  and proliferated into energy-rich cosmic niches as we are prone
  to do. But there is no reason to believe this (wouldn't it be
  arrogant?) based on what we know of the general behaviour of
  far-from-equilibrium organic systems. And if "they" are here
  because of the exploratory curiosity that you suggest then they
  do indeed behave like us. Too much like us perhaps, and too
  little like the cosmos-spanning superspecies that, if life were
  commonplace, could by now to have transformed the galaxies. On
  the other hand if life is so rarely seeded that we ought not to
  expect its spores to have colonised very widely, what is so much
  of it apparently doing flying around Earth here and now?
  I don't say that any of these premises or inferences are cast
  iron. But they deserve thinking about and making clearer. It is
  not just a lot of old off-the-wall wild-assed baloney that we
  should wave off with contempt. Fermi had a point.
